labels.reason: Historical reviewer: 'Certainly' as an adverb of degree or sentence adverb is standard human English ('Certainly they will learn more', 'Certainly schools should teach', 'Is it much harder... Certainly, but...'). It is not a chat-scaffold word — it appears throughout Paul Graham essays and journalistic prose as a normal emphatic or concessive adverb. The chat-scaffold pattern it is supposed to catch ('Certainly! Here is...') requires an exclamation mark and an imperative follow-on, not a bare adverb in flowing prose.
